title: Coding Adventure: Simulating an Ecosystem
beats: Map with water, land, trees and plants, then a crude cube bunny hopping about
Give him hunger and thirst; watch him find water and plants; sensory radius shown as limit of what he sees
Urge to reproduce is stronger than hunger; he searches in vain, so add a female
Mating scene with 'avert your eyes'; offspring grow and develop speed and sight
List the genes: gestation, sensory distance, reproductive urge, speed, desirability (redder fur)
Peek at the code: male signals, desirability sets acceptance, rejected females get remembered then forgotten; inheritance picks from parent or mutates
Start 300 rabbits; population spikes, crashes, extinction risk, then recovers
After 20 minutes: 1,400 rabbits, 2,600 hunger deaths, 4,000 thirst deaths
Gene graphs: gestation steady, sight rises, urge dips then recovers, speed not worth it, desirability up; each given a reason
Add fox that hunts rabbits, then rabbits flee
Foxes hunt rabbits to extinction then starve; speed now valuable
Second run with foxes from the start: rabbits nearly die, rebound, fox boom, both extinct; urge gets very high
Rarely co-exist; happy ending where foxes lost the last bunnies

metrics.key_term: evolution through gene inheritance, mutation and selection pressure
metrics.examples: 1 bunny, 2 bunnies, 300 rabbits, then foxes in 2 runs; growth by adding one rule at a time
metrics.ending: Happy-ending joke about the last surviving bunnies, series plug

new_moves.name: add-one-rule-then-run
new_moves.what: Each new behaviour or entity is added then run until its consequence is visible before the next one

new_moves.name: explain-the-result-after-showing-it
new_moves.what: Shows gene trend graphs, then supplies a plausible one-line reason for each

theory: The ecosystem is built as a stack of single rules, each introduced right when its absence becomes visible (a lonely bunny needs a mate), and then run so the learner sees the consequence before any summary. Explanations of results come after the plots, so the learner first sees the pattern then hears a causal story. Agent as a named character makes abstract selection pressure feel like narrative.
velocity: Scene builder: rule-stacking sims with a toggle per rule so the tutor can add one rule at a time
Voice: narrate outcomes after the curve appears, as a hypothesis, with the 'I guess' hedge
Orchestrator: 'run it again' action for visible repetition with different starting conditions
Evals: check that each new parameter appears only after the learner has seen the symptom that motivates it
quote: You may want to avert your eyes for this
